title: Backward persistence of liveness
statement: Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on a Boolean input, and let $s\le t$ be natural numbers. If the configuration reached after $t$ steps has not halted, then the configuration reached after $s$ steps has not halted.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a multi-tape Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet
$c$ is a configuration on a Boolean input
The configuration reached after $t$ steps is not halted
replaced:
Let $M$ be a multi-tape Turing machine, $c$ one of its configurations on some
input, and $s \le t$ natural numbers.  If the configuration reached from $c$
after $t$ steps is not halted, then neither is the configuration reached
after $s$ steps: since halting is absorbing, a live later configuration
excludes all earlier halts.
